data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

extract_result.purpose: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy for the management requirements associated with the clearance of an information collection request (ICR). This guidance must be used when collecting information from the public, including individuals, businesses, other private institutions, and State and local governments.
extract_result.scope: This DR applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, and others who work for, or on behalf of, USDA that are involved with developing or processing information collection requests.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy for the management requirements associated with the clearance of an information collection request (ICR).
policy_statements.target: management requirements associated with the clearance of an information collection request (ICR)

policy_statements.source_text: This guidance must be used when collecting information from the public, including individuals, businesses, other private institutions, and State and local governments.
policy_statements.target: information from the public, including individuals, businesses, other private institutions, and State and local governments
conditions: when collecting information from the public

policy_statements.source_text: This DR supersedes DR 3410-001, Information Collection Activities – Collection of Information from the Public, dated May 6, 2009.
cross_references: DR 3410-001, Information Collection Activities – Collection of Information from the Public, dated May 6, 2009

policy_statements.source_text: This policy is effective immediately and remains in effect until it is superseded or it expires.
All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must align their policies and procedures with this DR within 6 months of the publication date.
policy_statements.actor_name: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: within 6 months of the publication date

policy_statements.source_text: This DR is not applicable to the collection of information from Federal employees or military personnel as part of their work-related duties.
policy_statements.target: collection of information from Federal employees or military personnel as part of their work-related duties
conditions: as part of their work-related duties

policy_statements.source_text: This DR applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, and others who work for, or on behalf of, USDA that are involved with developing or processing information collection requests.
policy_statements.target: all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, and others who work for, or on behalf of, USDA that are involved with developing or processing information collection requests
conditions: that are involved with developing or processing information collection requests

policy_statements.source_text: The Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA), Public Law (P.L.) 104-13 and its implementing regulation, 5 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 1320, Controlling Paperwork Burdens on the Public, were established in response to public complaints about the amount of paperwork burden imposed by the Federal Government on members of the public.
cross_references: Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA), Public Law (P.L.) 104-13
5 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 1320, Controlling Paperwork Burdens on the Public

policy_statements.source_text: Members of the public include, but are not limited to: individual people (including contractors), businesses, associations, and partnerships, State, tribal, and local governments, universities and foreign citizens, governments, and businesses.
The goals of the PRA are to:
Minimize the burden on the public when collecting information, especially by using technology;
Maximize the practical use of the information collected;
policy_statements.target: practical use of the information collected

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that an information collection does not duplicate already existing information, or duplicate effort;
Maximize the cooperation amongst Federal program areas and agencies;
policy_statements.target: cooperation amongst Federal program areas and agencies

policy_statements.source_text: Promote openness and accountability in the collection and use of information;
policy_statements.target: openness and accountability in the collection and use of information

policy_statements.source_text: Improve integrity, quality, security, and utility of information to all users within and outside the Federal Government; and
policy_statements.target: integrity, quality, security, and utility of information

policy_statements.source_text: Improve Federal responsibility and accountability.
The PRA requires every Federal agency, except those specifically exempted, to obtain approval from the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for any planned information collections.
conditions: except those specifically exempted

policy_statements.source_text: Approved collections must be renewed at least every 3 years.
conditions: at least every 3 years

policy_statements.source_text: Collected information must:
Be essential to the Mission Area’s, agency’s, or staff office’s mission and have demonstrated practical use for the office in performing its function; and
Be collected in the most efficient, effective, and economical manner possible.
Approval and clearance is required for voluntary collections, mandatory collections, and collections required to obtain a Federal benefit (e.g., jobs, grants, permits.)
policy_statements.target: voluntary collections, mandatory collections, and collections required to obtain a Federal benefit

policy_statements.source_text: An information collection needs clearance if Mission Areas, agencies, or staff offices are collecting information in order to:

Obtain facts or opinions from 10 or more persons within a 12-month period by the use of standard questions or reporting requirements presented in forms, telephone or personal interviews, surveys, questionnaires, and web pages; requests for narrative responses to questions; requests for identical information, or almost any other means;
policy_statements.target: facts or opinions from 10 or more persons within a 12-month period

policy_statements.source_text: Require members of the public to provide information to the general public or to a third party;
Impose any requirements to label or mark items or packaging;
Require use of technological methods, including automated techniques, to monitor public compliance with Government requirements; or
Require compilation or maintenance of records, either alone or in conjunction with, the reporting of information.
Examples of information collections that require OMB clearance are:
Grant applications and reports if information is collected other than by use of, or in addition to, Standard Forms (e.g., narrative proposals, supporting documentation, performance reports);
conditions: if information is collected other than by use of, or in addition to, Standard Forms

policy_statements.source_text: Written reports (e.g., special use, grantee performance reports);
Surveys (e.g., in person, online, or telephone visitor surveys, customer surveys);
Forms (e.g., visitor use reports, IRS 1040).
Examples of information collections that do not require OMB clearance are:
Requests or collections from fewer than 10 members of the public;
Open-ended requests for comments or feedback;
Collections from Federal employees or military personnel as part of their work duties;
Discussions and questions from a public hearing, meeting, or online equivalent;
Some Federal investigations and civil actions, antitrust actions, and intelligence activities.
Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices conducting or sponsoring an information collection are responsible for obtaining OMB approval.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: conducting or sponsoring an information collection

policy_statements.source_text: An information collection is considered to be “conducted” if the information being collected is done using USDA staff and resources.
conditions: if the information being collected is done using USDA staff and resources

policy_statements.source_text: An information collection is considered to be “sponsored” if another agency is used to collect information, enters into a contract or a cooperative agreement with another person to collect information, or requires a person to provide information to another person, or otherwise causes another person to obtain, retain, solicit, or require the disclosure to third parties or the public of information by or for a USDA organization.
conditions: if another agency is used to collect information, enters into a contract or a cooperative agreement with another person to collect information, or requires a person to provide information to another person, or otherwise causes another person to obtain, retain, solicit, or require the disclosure to third parties or the public of information by or for a USDA organization

policy_statements.source_text: USDA must provide members of the public with the option to submit information, transact business, and maintain records by paper or electronically when feasible.
conditions: when feasible

policy_statements.source_text: This will provide OMB with information on how to assess both compliance with PRA and the E-Government Act of 2002, P.L. 107-347.
Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices cannot ask members of the public to respond to a collection that does not have OMB approval.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: that does not have OMB approval

policy_statements.source_text: If doing so, they are in violation of the PRA.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: If doing so

policy_statements.source_text: By failing to comply, Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices:
Could open USDA and the information collected to legal challenge; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: By failing to comply

policy_statements.source_text: Will have the violations of the PRA reported to Congress and the President in the Information Collection Budget (ICB).
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: By failing to comply

policy_statements.source_text: Title III of the E-Government Act, also known as the Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA), requires Federal agencies to ensure the security of the information and information systems that support the operations and assets of the agency, including those provided or managed by another agency, contractor, or other source.
policy_statements.target: security of the information and information systems that support the operations and assets of the agency, including those provided or managed by another agency, contractor, or other source
cross_references: Title III of the E-Government Act
Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA)

policy_statements.source_text: Federal agencies and their contractors must comply with FISMA standards and obtain an Authority to Operate (ATO) appropriate for the types of information which reside on these information systems.
They must also ensure that a Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) is competed for these systems as well.

So that agencies and their contractors are aware of and prepare to meet the legal requirements for their information systems before initiating a new information collection, the following information should be completed:
Both ATO and PIA (if PII is collected) requirements apply to information systems of Federal agencies and their contractors (e.g., in the private sector and academia);
policy_statements.target: information systems of Federal agencies and their contractors
conditions: if PII is collected

policy_statements.source_text: An ATO that is commensurate with the appropriate FISMA compliance level(s) is required, even if PII is not collected by an information collection; and
policy_statements.target: ATO that is commensurate with the appropriate FISMA compliance level(s)
conditions: even if PII is not collected by an information collection

policy_statements.source_text: An information collection cannot begin if the information system that will be used to conduct or host the collected information does not have an appropriate ATO, even if an agency obtains OMB clearance for the collection.
conditions: if the information system that will be used to conduct or host the collected information does not have an appropriate ATO
even if an agency obtains OMB clearance for the collection

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will demonstrate in their OMB clearance package submissions that the ICR will result in information that complies with OMB and USDA Information Quality Guidelines when collecting information that requires OMB clearance under PRA.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: when collecting information that requires OMB clearance under PRA
cross_references: OMB and USDA Information Quality Guidelines

policy_statements.source_text: For additional information on PRA, see OMB’s Federal Collection of Information web page.
cross_references: OMB’s Federal Collection of Information web page

policy_statements.source_text: For additional information on Privacy, see OMB’s Privacy web page.

OMB requires each Federal agency to submit an annual information collection budget (ICB) estimating the hours of burden to be imposed on the public in the next fiscal year and verifying accomplishments in prior years.
Each year, OMB determines the ICB format, reduction goals, and other required inputs.
policy_statements.target: ICB format, reduction goals, and other required inputs
conditions: Each year

policy_statements.source_text: To achieve reduction goals, Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must carefully review their rules and regulations.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: They also must be prepared to offset increases in some collections by identifying decreases in others.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices should plan their ICR needs 6 months or more in advance and expect strict adherence to the estimates for new ICRs that were submitted in the ICB.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: They must be prepared to reduce other proposed or existing collections if unexpected new collections are needed during the fiscal year to keep the new burden at or below the approved levels.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: if unexpected new collections are needed during the fiscal year

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must provide a report for regulatory actions requiring a paperwork burden (e.g., notice of proposed rulemaking, interim final rule, or final rule.)
policy_statements.target: regulatory actions requiring a paperwork burden

policy_statements.source_text: Further information can be found in DR 1512-001, Regulatory Development and Review.
If a regulatory action involves paperwork burden, the Mission Area, agency, or staff office must:
conditions: If a regulatory action involves paperwork burden

policy_statements.source_text: Clear it with the appropriate program personnel and Mission Area, agency, or staff office Agency Information Collection Officer (AICO);
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, or staff office

policy_statements.source_text: Prepare and input data into the Regulatory and Information Service Center (RISC) Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA) Consolidated Information System (ROCIS); and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, or staff office
policy_statements.target: Regulatory and Information Service Center (RISC) Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA) Consolidated Information System (ROCIS)

policy_statements.source_text: Submit one electronic copy of the ICR to the Departmental Information Collection Officer (DICO) at least 15 business days prior to the publication of the regulatory action.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, or staff office
conditions: at least 15 business days prior to the publication of the regulatory action

policy_statements.source_text: The DICO must transmit the ICR to OMB through ROCIS or notify the sponsoring Mission Area, agency, or staff office if the package needs editing or does not contain all required information.
conditions: if the package needs editing or does not contain all required information

policy_statements.source_text: If an ICR pertains to rulemaking, the Mission Area, agency, or staff office must publish a notice in the Federal Register to inform the public of OMB’s decision on the ICR.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, or staff office

Serve as the central point of contact for communications with OMB concerning the ICR;
policy_statements.target: communications with OMB concerning the ICR

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that the ICR contains all required information;
Serve as the liaisons to OMB on ICR management clearances and activities;

policy_statements.target: Departmental ICR management policy, objectives, standards, and guidelines

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that ICRs comply with the legal requirements of the PRA, E-Government Act, and the Privacy Act, as applicable, to reduce, minimize, and control burden; protect sensitive information; and maximize practical use and public benefit;
conditions: as applicable

policy_statements.source_text: Provide monthly reports to AICOs showing ICRs expiring within the next 12 months;

Review each ICR to ensure consistency with USDA and OMB policy, appropriateness of the statistical designs for proposed information collections, practical utility of the information being collected, as well as:
Ensure that an ICR is necessary; and
Encourage consolidation of collections and forms when practicable;
conditions: when practicable

policy_statements.source_text: Review and submit new ICRs in ROCIS to OMB, and extensions and revisions of currently approved ICRs before their expiration dates;
policy_statements.target: new ICRs in ROCIS to OMB, and extensions and revisions of currently approved ICRs

Review and clear PRA section in regulatory actions for any paperwork burden;

before submitting to OCIO

when respondents submit proprietary or other confidential information

a. The *Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995* (PRA), Public Law ( P.L.) 104-13  and its implementing regulation,  5 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 1320 , *Controlling Paperwork Burdens on the Public*, were established in response to public complaints about the amount of paperwork burden imposed by the Federal Government on members of the public. Members of the public include, but are not limited to: individual people (including contractors), businesses, associations, and partnerships, State, tribal, and local governments, universities and foreign citizens, governments, and businesses.

Members of the public include, but are not limited to: individual people (including contractors), businesses, associations, and partnerships, State, tribal, and local governments, universities and foreign citizens, governments, and businesses.
The goals of the PRA are to:
Minimize the burden on the public when collecting information, especially by using technology;
Maximize the practical use of the information collected;
practical use of the information collected
Ensure that an information collection does not duplicate already existing information, or duplicate effort;
Maximize the cooperation amongst Federal program areas and agencies;
cooperation amongst Federal program areas and agencies
Promote openness and accountability in the collection and use of information;
openness and accountability in the collection and use of information
Improve integrity, quality, security, and utility of information to all users within and outside the Federal Government; and
integrity, quality, security, and utility of information
The PRA requires every Federal agency, except those specifically exempted, to obtain approval from the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for any planned information collections.
Approved collections must be renewed at least every 3 years.
Be essential to the Mission Area’s, agency’s, or staff office’s mission and have demonstrated practical use for the office in performing its function; and
Be collected in the most efficient, effective, and economical manner possible.
Approval and clearance is required for voluntary collections, mandatory collections, and collections required to obtain a Federal benefit (e.g., jobs, grants, permits.)
voluntary collections, mandatory collections, and collections required to obtain a Federal benefit
An information collection needs clearance if Mission Areas, agencies, or staff offices are collecting information in order to:

Obtain facts or opinions from 10 or more persons within a 12-month period by the use of standard questions or reporting requirements presented in forms, telephone or personal interviews, surveys, questionnaires, and web pages; requests for narrative responses to questions; requests for identical information, or almost any other means;
facts or opinions from 10 or more persons within a 12-month period
Require members of the public to provide information to the general public or to a third party;
Impose any requirements to label or mark items or packaging;
Require use of technological methods, including automated techniques, to monitor public compliance with Government requirements; or
Require compilation or maintenance of records, either alone or in conjunction with, the reporting of information.
Examples of information collections that require OMB clearance are:
Grant applications and reports if information is collected other than by use of, or in addition to, Standard Forms (e.g., narrative proposals, supporting documentation, performance reports);
if information is collected other than by use of, or in addition to, Standard Forms
Written reports (e.g., special use, grantee performance reports);
Surveys (e.g., in person, online, or telephone visitor surveys, customer surveys);
Examples of information collections that do not require OMB clearance are:
Requests or collections from fewer than 10 members of the public;
Open-ended requests for comments or feedback;
Collections from Federal employees or military personnel as part of their work duties;
Discussions and questions from a public hearing, meeting, or online equivalent;
Some Federal investigations and civil actions, antitrust actions, and intelligence activities.
Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices conducting or sponsoring an information collection are responsible for obtaining OMB approval.

Title III of the *E-Government Act*, also known as the  *Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014*  (FISMA), requires Federal agencies to ensure the security of the information and information systems that support the operations and assets of the agency, including those provided or managed by another agency, contractor, or other source.
